To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the combination of deep convolutional networks and unsupervised feature learners is an effective approach for scene text recognition and (ii) a simple lexicon driven search is a powerful method for decoding the results from the recognition module, which is a significant improvement compared to previous methods that relied on sophisticated postprocessing methods.

(1) a convolutional neural network trained on a combination of synthetic and real images can learn powerful text detectors and character classifiers; (2) these modules can be integrated into a full end-to-end text recognition system that outperforms the previous state of the art by a large margin.

(i) deep neural networks can be trained to detect and recognize text in natural images, (ii) deep convolutional neural networks can be used to extract features for text recognition, and (iii) unsupervised feature learners are effective at learning features for text recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How can we train large multilayer networks to recognize characters in natural images? (2) How can we use the output of such networks to train a text detector?
the following two questions: How can we use deep learning to improve text detection? How can we use unsupervised feature discovery to improve text recognition?
developing an end to end text detector and recognizer for images of natural scenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a novel approach to scene text recognition which is based on deep convolutional neural networks and achieves state of the-art results on standard benchmarks.

we are able to achieve state of the art results on standard benchmarks, and our system outperforms previous systems on the Street View Text dataset by a margin of 2.7 points, and on the ICDAR 3rd word accuracy challenge by a margin of over 4.5 points.
our method is a state of the art method for scene text recognition, and it is the first to achieve end to end recognition without the need for any hand crafted features or prior knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved state of the art results in end to end text detection and recognition in natural scenes, without the need for any hand engineered features or elaborate models.

we show that a simple, end to end, text recognition system that uses only a few hundred parameters and is trained entirely from scratch can perform on par or better than the current state of the art systems that are much more complex.

we have shown that end to end recognition of text in natural images is feasible with a single, unified, deep neural network architecture, trained in an end to end manner, with no need for any elaborate feature engineering or prior knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, end to end, text recognition system can be trained from data alone, without the need for elaborate feature engineering or prior knowledge.
a simple, end to end system, that uses no prior knowledge about text or scene context, can be trained to recognize text in natural images.

, in spite of their simplicity, the proposed end to end text recognizer achieves state of the Art accuracy and can be trained from scratch without using any hand engineered features or any form of external knowledge.
